item: C1 of data/pilot/194/novelty.json: Thm 2.1 (complex.tex:55-82), the uniform estimate for free complexes with deep differential entries under an abstract additive length: lambda H_0(F) >= mu s^h (b_0 - A_h/s * sum_i b_i).
item_statement: C a commutative ring (not necessarily Noetherian), I = (z_1..z_h), lambda an additive [0,inf]-valued length on I-power-torsion modules, with lambda(0)=0 and zero-stability (direct sums and filtered colimits of length-zero modules killed by a common I^a have length zero). Assume 0 < mu = lambda(C/I) < inf, lambda(C/(z^a)) = a^h mu, and lambda H_i(z^a; C) = 0 for i > 0. Let F be a complex of finite free modules in degrees 0..h, contractible locally off V(I), with b_i = rank F_i. Then H_i(F) is I-power torsion, lambda H_i(F) = 0 for i>0 and lambda H_0(F) < inf. If moreover sum (-1)^i b_i = 0 and every differential entry lies in I^s (s >= 1), then lambda H_0(F) >= mu s^h (b_0 - A_h/s * sum b_i), with A_h depending only on h. Proof: pass to the blowup Y of I (Rees charts), divide the differentials by L^s to get G_i = O(-is)^{b_i}, tensor with an Eisenbud-Schreyer-type bundle whose roots sit at rounded s*rho_j (rho_j the roots of H'(x), H = prod_{i=1}^h (x+i)), force the hyperhomology into degree 0 modulo length zero (chi >= 0), compare chi with lambda H_0(F), and isolate b_0 using equal leading layer sums plus alternating rank 0.
item_type: F5/F3 (a uniform estimate, produced by a construction: blowup twist plus supernatural-bundle pairing with tuned roots). The ES bundle itself is N0 transfer; the device is the estimate and its mechanism.
lean_status_why: OAI.Lech.complex_theorem (ComplexTheorem.lean:26) is Thm 2.1 with the same hypotheses (h = n+1 parameters, ZeroStability, 0 < mu < inf, parameter scaling and Koszul length-zero hypotheses, LocallyContractibleOff I F, alternating rank 0, entries in I^s, constant A depending only on n), proved along the paper's route (Rees-chart Cech model of the blowup, an Eisenbud-Schreyer-type root bundle via ProductSourceCover, roots floor(s*rho_j) of H'); the on-chain variant complex_estimate_basis (ComplexEstimate.lean:22) is the same estimate under slightly weaker hypotheses.
lean_gaps: Line reference: novelty.json cites ComplexEstimate.lean:88; the declaration is at line 22 (the file has 82 lines). 194_lean.json also gives line 22.
Indexing: Lean uses cochain complexes in degrees -(n+1)..0 with n+1 generators z : Fin (n+1) -> R; the paper uses homological degrees 0..h with h generators (h = n+1). Same content.

Hypotheses in the on-chain form: complex_estimate_basis needs only DirectSumZero (no filtered-colimit stability), drops 0 < mu, requires Nontrivial R and an explicit basis per term, and replaces 'contractible locally off V(I)' by 'acyclic after inverting each z_k' (equivalent for bounded finite free complexes; complex_theorem bridges via LocallyContractibleOff.acyclicAway). So the Lean on the chain is marginally STRONGER than the paper's statement.

The comparator only exercises the item through complex_estimate_allModule (AllModuleLength: a length on all C-modules with direct-sum, iSup and direct-limit stability), instantiated in char p with the normalized length on the perfection (exists_length_with_module_limit). The general TorsionLength version is proved, but the mixed-characteristic use (CLMST perfectoid lengths, mixed.tex:270) is not formalized.

No scheme-theoretic blowup: Y, L = O(1) and the exceptional divisor E are modelled by Cech complexes on the Rees-algebra charts (Chart n), filtered Rees denominators and an explicit exceptional fibre (ExceptionalFibre*, ReesRoot*, about 2.8k lines). The supernatural bundle is rebuilt over Z through the cover (P^1)^n -> P^n (ProductSourceCover*, 6 files, about 2.8k lines). Route-equivalent to the paper, not a different proof.

Size: the upstream closure of complex_estimate_basis is 2,679 declarations, about 20,900 lines in 163 files, i.e. 77% of the 3,499-declaration and about 32,000-line comparator DAG. The numerical root step (uniform_from_sum_estimate) is only 38 declarations / about 470 lines; the acyclicity half (SourceGraded.acyclicity_finite_torsion) is 91 declarations / about 880 lines. Almost all of the device's weight is the blowup-pairing positivity (sum_estimate closure: 2,641 declarations).
The constant A is existential (exists A >= 0), as in the paper; A absorbs the threshold on s, so the Lean bound holds for every s >= 1.

Comparator weaker than headline: the comparator is OAI.Lech.dutta_domain (IMW2022 Conj 8.1 for complete local DOMAINS of char p plus convergence of the Dutta sequence). Lech's conjecture itself is not stated in Lean. Conversely the chain theorem dutta_complete_charp (DuttaDomain.lean:22) has NO IsDomain hypothesis: Lean proves multiplicity R <= duttaMultiplicity R p F for every complete Noetherian local ring of char p (prime filtration in CyclicDutta.lean), which is more than the comparator asks.

.obj F).Acyclic), (∀ i,powerTorsion I (F.homology i) ∧ ell.value (F.homology i)≠⊤) ∧ (∀ i : ℤ,i≠0 → ell.value (F.homology i)=0) ∧ ∀ s : ℕ,0

lean_source.text:
theorem complex_estimate_allModule (d : ℕ) (hd : 0<d) :
    ∃ A : ℝ,0≤A ∧ ∀ {C : Type u} [CommRing C] [Nontrivial C]
      (z : Fin d → C) (ell : AllModuleLength C) (e : ℝ) (_he : 0≤e)
      (_hmu : ell.value (ModuleCat.of C (C ⧸ Ideal.span (Set.range z))) = ENNReal.ofReal e)
      (_ha : ∀ a : ℕ,0<a → ell.value (ModuleCat.of C
        (C ⧸ Ideal.span (Set.range (fun j => z j^a)))) = (a:ℝ≥0∞)^d*ENNReal.ofReal e)
      (_hK : ∀ a : ℕ,1≤a → ∀ i : ℤ,i < 0 →
        ell.value ((Koszul.unit (List.ofFn (fun j => z j^a))).homology i)=0)
      (F : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} C) ℤ)
      (_hf : ∀ i,Module.Free C (F.X i)) (_hfin : ∀ i,Module.Finite C (F.X i))
      (_hb : ∀ i,i < -(d:ℤ) ∨ 0 < i → IsZero (F.X i))
      (_hac : ∀ j,(((baseChangeFunctor C (Localization.Away (z j))).mapHomologicalComplex _).obj F).Acyclic)
      (s : ℕ) (_hs : 0<s)
      (_hδ : ∀ i : ℤ,(F.d i (i+1)).hom.range ≤
        (Ideal.span (Set.range z))^s • (⊤ : Submodule C (F.X (i+1))))
      (_halt : ∑ i∈Finset.range (d+1),(-1:ℝ)^i*(Module.finrank C (F.X (-(i:ℤ))):ℝ)=0),
      e*(s:ℝ)^d*((Module.finrank C (F.X 0):ℝ)-A/s*
        ∑ i∈Finset.range (d+1),(Module.finrank C (F.X (-(i:ℤ))):ℝ)) ≤
          (ell.value (F.homology 0)).toReal
lean_source.role: item as consumed by the comparator (AllModuleLength, I = span z); on the chain

lean_source.name: OAI.Lech.TorsionLength
lean_source.text:
structure TorsionLength (I : Ideal R) where
  value : ModuleCat.{u} R → ℝ≥0∞
  zero : ∀ {M}, IsZero M → value M = 0
  additive : ∀ {S : ShortComplex (ModuleCat.{u} R)}, S.ShortExact →
    powerTorsion I S.X₂ → value S.X₂ = value S.X₁ + value S.X₃
lean_source.role: defining structure: additive length on I-power-torsion modules

lean_source.name: OAI.Lech.powerTorsion
lean_source.text:
def powerTorsion (I : Ideal R) : ObjectProperty (ModuleCat.{u} R) :=
  fun M => ∃ n : ℕ, I ^ n ≤ Module.annihilator R M

lean_source.name: OAI.Lech.TorsionLength.DirectSumZero
lean_source.text:
def TorsionLength.DirectSumZero (ell : TorsionLength I) : Prop :=
  ∀ {ι : Type u} (M : ι → Type u) [∀ i, AddCommGroup (M i)] [∀ i, Module R (M i)]
    (a : ℕ), (∀ i, I^a ≤ Module.annihilator R (M i)) →
      (∀ i, ell.value (ModuleCat.of R (M i))=0) → ell.value (ModuleCat.of R (⨁ i, M i))=0
lean_source.role: zero-stability for direct sums (the only stability hypothesis complex_estimate_basis needs)

lean_source.name: OAI.Lech.TorsionLength.FilteredColimitZero
lean_source.text:
def TorsionLength.FilteredColimitZero (ell : TorsionLength I) : Prop :=
  ∀ {J : Type u} [SmallCategory J] [IsFiltered J] (D : J ⥤ ModuleCat.{u} R)
    (a : ℕ), (∀ j,I^a ≤ Module.annihilator R (D.obj j)) →
      (∀ j,ell.value (D.obj j)=0) → ell.value (colimit D)=0
lean_source.role: zero-stability for filtered colimits (paper hypothesis; not needed by complex_estimate_basis)

lean_source.name: OAI.Lech.TorsionLength.ZeroStability
lean_source.text:
def TorsionLength.ZeroStability (ell : TorsionLength I) : Prop :=
  ell.DirectSumZero ∧ ell.FilteredColimitZero

lean_source.name: OAI.Lech.AllModuleLength
lean_source.text:
structure AllModuleLength (C : Type u) [CommRing C] where
  value : ModuleCat.{u} C → ℝ≥0∞
  zero : ∀ {M}, IsZero M → value M = 0
  additive : ∀ {S : ShortComplex (ModuleCat.{u} C)}, S.ShortExact →
    value S.X₂ = value S.X₁ + value S.X₃
  directSum_zero : ∀ {ι : Type u} (G : ι → Type u) [∀ i, AddCommGroup (G i)]
    [∀ i, Module C (G i)],
    (∀ i, value (ModuleCat.of C (G i)) = 0) → value (ModuleCat.of C (⨁ i, G i)) = 0
  iSup_zero : ∀ {ι M : Type u} [AddCommGroup M] [Module C M]
    (U : ι → Submodule C M),
    (∀ i, value (ModuleCat.of C (U i)) = 0) →
      value (ModuleCat.of C (⨆ i, U i : Submodule C M)) = 0
  directLimit_zero : ∀ {ι : Type u} [Preorder ι] [Nonempty ι] [IsDirectedOrder ι]
    (G : ι → Type u) [∀ i, AddCommGroup (G i)] [∀ i, Module C (G i)]
    (g : ∀ i j, i ≤ j → G i →ₗ[C] G j),
    (∀ i, value (ModuleCat.of C (G i)) = 0) →
      value (ModuleCat.of C (Module.DirectLimit G g)) = 0
lean_source.role: length on all modules (used by the comparator wrapper; normalized perfection length in char p)

lean_source.name: OAI.Lech.ReesRoot.rootTotal_euler_nonnegative
lean_source.text:
theorem rootTotal_euler_nonnegative (r : Fin n → ℤ) (hr : RootPositions n s r)
    (N : ℕ) (hN : n+1≤N) :
    let D := (enlargedAt I z hz F (n+1) s hd (rootAmbient s r 0)).total (.up ℤ)
    (∀ i,ell.finiteClass (D.homology i)) ∧
      (-1:ℝ)^(n+1)*finiteHomologyEuler ell D (-(n+1:ℤ)) N=ell.realValue (D.homology 0) ∧
      0≤(-1:ℝ)^(n+1)*finiteHomologyEuler ell D (-(n+1:ℤ)) N
lean_source.role: key lemma: hyperhomology of G (x) V concentrated in degree 0 modulo length zero, so chi >= 0 (complex.tex eq complex-positive-chi)

lean_source.name: OAI.Lech.ReesRoot.sum_estimate
lean_source.text:
theorem sum_estimate (r : Fin n → ℤ) (hr : RootPositions n s r) :
    0≤(n.factorial:ℝ)*ell.realValue (F.homology 0)+
      ell.realValue (ModuleCat.of R (R ⧸ I))*
        ∑ i∈Finset.range (n+2),(-1:ℝ)^i*(b (-(i:ℤ)):ℝ)*rootStripPolynomial n r i s
lean_source.role: key lemma: the pairing inequality 0 <= h! * lambda H_0 + mu * sum (-1)^i b_i layer_i (complex.tex eq complex-sum-estimate), with h-1 = n roots

lean_source.name: OAI.Lech.ProductSourceCover.RootPositions
lean_source.text:
def RootPositions (s : ℕ) (r : Fin n → ℤ) : Prop :=
  ∀ j, -((j.val:ℤ)+2)*(s:ℤ) < r j ∧ r j < -((j.val:ℤ)+1)*(s:ℤ)

lean_source.name: OAI.Lech.Numerical.roundedRoot
lean_source.text:
noncomputable def roundedRoot (n s : ℕ) (j : Fin n) : ℤ :=
  ⌊(s : ℝ) * ρ n j⌋
lean_source.role: roots r_j = floor(s * rho_j), rho_j the roots of H'(x), H = prod(x+i)

lean_source.name: OAI.Lech.Numerical.uniform_from_sum_estimate
lean_source.text:
theorem uniform_from_sum_estimate (n : ℕ) :
    ∃ A : ℝ, 0 ≤ A ∧ ∀ (s : ℕ), 0 < s → ∀ (b : Fin (n+2) → ℝ),
      (∀ i, 0 ≤ b i) → ∀ (μ L : ℝ), 0 ≤ μ → 0 ≤ L →
      (∑ i, (-1:ℝ)^i.val*b i=0) →
      (GoodRoots n s → 0 ≤ (n.factorial:ℝ)*L+
        μ*∑ i, (-1:ℝ)^i.val*b i*layer n i.val s) →
      μ*(s:ℝ)^(n+1)*(b 0-A/s*∑ i,b i) ≤ L
lean_source.role: numerical step: equal layer sums isolate b_0 with coefficient 1 and O(1/s) error

lean_source.name: OAI.Lech.CharP.dutta_minimal_estimate
lean_source.text:
theorem dutta_minimal_estimate (hd : 0 < dimension D)
    (F : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} D) ℤ) (hF : IsFiniteHomologyComplex D F)
    (hm : IsMinimalComplex F) :
    ∃ (A : ℝ) (c : ℕ),0≤A ∧ ∀ n : ℕ,c < p^n →
      multiplicity D*((p^n-c:ℕ):ℝ)^dimension D*
        ((Module.finrank D (F.X 0):ℝ)-A/((p^n-c:ℕ):ℝ)*
          ∑ i∈Finset.range (dimension D+1),(Module.finrank D (F.X (-(i:ℤ))):ℝ)) ≤
            ((p:ℝ)^n)^dimension D*duttaMultiplicity D p F
lean_source.role: first consumer on the comparator chain (Frobenius, s = p^n - c)

lean_source.name: OAI.Lech.dutta_complete_charp
lean_source.text:
lemma dutta_complete_charp (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    [IsLocalRing R] [IsAdicComplete (maximalIdeal R) R]
    (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] [CharP R p]
    (F : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} R) ℤ) (hF : IsShortComplex R F) :
    (∀ n i,IsFiniteLength R ((frobeniusComplex R p n F).homology i)) ∧
      Tendsto (duttaSequence R p F) atTop (𝓝 (duttaMultiplicity R p F)) ∧
      multiplicity R ≤ duttaMultiplicity R p F
lean_source.role: comparator-chain theorem; NOTE no IsDomain hypothesis (Lean proves the Dutta bound for every complete Noetherian local ring of char p)

speedup_targets.title: IMW 2022: Dutta multiplicity >= e(R) for localized standard graded algebras in char p
speedup_targets.statement: Let R be the localization at the homogeneous maximal ideal of a standard graded algebra over a field of characteristic p > 0 (perfect residue field as in IMW). For every short complex F over R (finite free, length <= dim R, finite-length homology, H_0 != 0), chi_infty(F) >= e(R).
speedup_targets.reference: Iyengar-Ma-Walker, 'Multiplicities and Betti numbers in local algebra via lim Ulrich points', Algebra Number Theory 16 (2022) 1213-1257, arXiv:2104.10140 (main Dutta-multiplicity theorem; exact theorem number unverified, abstract read via search snippet only)
speedup_targets.status: known (proved via lim Ulrich sequences built from sheaves on Proj)
speedup_targets.current_proof_size: IMW 2022 is about 45 pages; the Dutta part needs the lim Ulrich construction on the projective variety (several sections). No formalization anywhere.
speedup_targets.how_item_helps: Completion is a flat local map with mS = n, preserving dimension, e and chi_infty (DuttaBaseChange.lean / multiplicity_eq_of_map_maximalIdeal already do this for residue extensions). Then dutta_complete_charp (no domain hypothesis) gives the bound. With the item in L the proof is glue (completion is complete Noetherian local of char p); without it there is no short route (the lim-Ulrich proof is long and uses graded geometry absent from Mathlib).
speedup_targets.counts_as_device_reuse: no: corollary of the comparator theorem (IMW Conj 8.1 in char p), hence a theorem corollary. Use only to calibrate the harness and to show that the device subsumes the lim-Ulrich route.

speedup_targets.title: IMW length bound l(M) >= e(R) over complete intersections in char p
speedup_targets.statement: Let R be a complete intersection local ring of characteristic p > 0 and M a nonzero finite-length R-module of finite projective dimension. Then l(M) >= e(R) (indeed >= beta_0(M) e(R)).
speedup_targets.reference: IMW 2022 prove l(M) >= e(R) for STRICT complete intersections (arXiv:2104.10140, snippet); Dutta 1983 (Compositio) / Kurano 2004 (arXiv:math/0304220): chi_infty = chi on complete intersections, more generally exactly on numerically Roberts rings
speedup_targets.status: strict-CI case known; the general char-p complete-intersection case may be new (UNVERIFIED: not checked against KC-Soto Levins 2024 or later work)
speedup_targets.current_proof_size: IMW strict-CI argument: Ulrich modules over strict CIs, a few pages on top of their framework. No formalization.
speedup_targets.how_item_helps: Minimal resolution F of M is short (Auslander-Buchsbaum: length = depth = dim). On a CI, chi_infty(F) = chi(F) = l(M). The item's Dutta consequence (with the b_0 factor kept: chi_infty >= b_0 e(R), charp.tex:244-253) gives l(M) >= beta_0(M) e(R) at once.

speedup_targets.counts_as_device_reuse: no: corollary of the Dutta corollary plus Dutta/Kurano's chi_infty = chi. Record as reach.

speedup_verdict: No strong device-reuse speedup target found. Every KNOWN theorem that the estimate shortens a lot is reached through the Dutta bound chi_infty >= e(R) (IMW Conj 8.1 in char p), i.e. it is a theorem corollary. The coefficient 1 is what makes the estimate matter, and coefficient 1 is needed only for e(R)-sharp statements (Lech, Dutta >= e, length >= e). Weaker known statements (New Intersection Theorem, positivity of Dutta multiplicity) do not need the device at all (see negative_controls). The one release family that touches the machinery (193) reuses only the routine acyclicity half.

open_problems.title: Local pure-type estimate with non-uniform depths (local Herzog-Kuhl / HHS lower bound)
open_problems.statement: Same setting as Thm 2.1 but the i-th differential has entries in I^{s_i} (s_i >= 1 not all equal). Put d_i = s_1+...+s_i. Is lambda H_0(F) >= mu b_0 prod_{i=1}^h d_i / h! * (1 - o(1)) as min s_i -> infinity, uniformly in C, lambda, F? For s_i = s this is exactly Thm 2.1 (prod(is)/h! = s^h). The graded analogue for pure resolutions is the Herzog-Kuhl / Huneke-Miller formula l(M) = b_0 prod d_i / h!, and its non-pure form is the HHS lower bound proved by Eisenbud-Schreyer.
open_problems.reference: Posed here as a device test. Background: Eisenbud-Schreyer, JAMS 22 (2009) (HHS lower bound via pairing); Herzog-Kuhl 1984; Herzog-Srinivasan, Trans. AMS 350 (1998) (multiplicity conjecture); BEKS, 'Shapes of free resolutions over a local ring', Math. Ann. (2012), arXiv:1105.2244
open_problems.status: open as far as found: searches for a local HHS-type bound in terms of m-adic depth of the differentials returned only graded results (snippet level; UNVERIFIED)
open_problems.obstruction_match: Exactly the item's obstruction: a coefficient-sharp lower bound on H_0 of a local, ungraded complex from the depth of its differentials, where passing to associated graded rings loses exactness (MaUlrich Remark 3.9).
open_problems.adaptation_sketch: On the blowup, divide d_i by L^{s_i} so G_i = O(-d_i)^{b_i}; pair with a bundle whose roots are chosen as in Eisenbud-Schreyer for the pure degree sequence (0, d_1, ..., d_h) instead of the uniform one; the layer-sum computation (NumericalSupport) must be redone for the new layer polynomial. The positivity half (rootTotal_euler_nonnegative) should transfer once RootPositions is generalized.
open_problems.payoff: med (a new local Boij-Soderberg-type inequality; also a clean test of reusing the DESIGN rather than the statement)
open_problems.difficulty: med (numerics of roots for unequal steps; the interlacing positions may fail for very unequal s_i)

open_problems.title: The IMW Length Conjecture: l(M) >= e(R) for modules of finite projective dimension
open_problems.statement: For a Cohen-Macaulay local ring R and every nonzero finite-length R-module M of finite projective dimension, l(M) >= e(R). It implies Lech's conjecture for CM rings (search summaries).
open_problems.reference: Iyengar-Ma-Walker, ANT 16 (2022), arXiv:2104.10140; Walker, talk 'How short can a module of finite projective dimension be?' (researchseminars.org/talk/FOTR/40); KC-Soto Levins, 'On liftings of modules of finite projective dimension', IMRN 2024, arXiv:2404.17572
open_problems.status: open (partial: rings with Ulrich modules or lim Ulrich sequences; strict complete intersections; Serre-liftable modules)
open_problems.obstruction_match: Partial. The item bounds lambda H_0 of a complex with DEEP entries; a minimal resolution of M has entries only in m. In char p Frobenius makes them deep, but then the item controls chi_infty(F), not l(M); the two agree exactly on numerically Roberts rings (Kurano). Non-Roberts CM rings exist in char p (dim 3 CM, dim 5 Gorenstein), so this is precisely where the device stops.
open_problems.adaptation_sketch: (i) char p, numerically Roberts R (complete intersections, dim <= 2): corollary, see speedup target 2 and theorem_corollaries. (ii) General CM R: need a length lambda on an auxiliary algebra C with lambda(H_0(F (x) C)) = l(M) and depth-amplification of the entries without Frobenius, e.g. via the paper's mixed-char root extensions. No concrete route found.
open_problems.payoff: high (the conjecture strengthens Lech for CM rings)

open_problems.title: Positivity and the e(R) bound for Dutta multiplicity outside characteristic p (Kurano-Roberts; IMW Conj 8.1)
open_problems.statement: For a short complex F over a local ring R of mixed or equal-zero characteristic, with Dutta multiplicity defined through local Chern characters (Roberts, Kurano), show chi_infty(F) > 0 (Kurano-Roberts) and chi_infty(F) >= e(R) (IMW Conj 8.1).
open_problems.reference: IMW 2022 Conj 8.1; Kurano, 'Numerical equivalence defined on Chow groups of Noetherian local rings', Invent. Math. 157 (2004), arXiv:math/0304220; KC-Soto Levins 2024 (states the positivity conjecture is open in mixed characteristic, snippet)
open_problems.status: open in mixed characteristic (per arXiv:2404.17572 snippet; UNVERIFIED in full)
open_problems.obstruction_match: Strong. It is the same inequality the item proves in char p, with Frobenius unavailable; the paper already replaces Frobenius in its Lech proof by roots of parameters, Heitmann's Briancon-Skoda and CLMST perfectoid lengths (mixed.tex:270 applies Thm 2.1 there).
open_problems.adaptation_sketch: Run the char-p argument of charp.tex:193-313 with the mixed-char length of Section 4: apply Thm 2.1 to F (x) C over a root extension with entries pushed into (z)^{q-h} by Briancon-Skoda, divide by the extension rank. The missing piece is an identity between the normalized lambda-limit of H_0 and the local-Chern-character Dutta multiplicity (in char p this is eq. dutta-h0 plus Frobenius scaling). Adams operations psi^k (Gillet-Soule, Kurano) scale the top local Chern character by k^d and may play Frobenius's role.
open_problems.payoff: high (would settle the Kurano-Roberts positivity conjecture and IMW Conj 8.1 in mixed characteristic; genuine device reuse outside the comparator's characteristic)

open_problems.title: Boij-Soderberg cones over local rings without lim Ulrich sequences
open_problems.statement: IMW 2023 compare the cone of Betti tables of finite-length, finite-projective-dimension modules over R with the cone over a (linear) Noether normalization, using lim Ulrich sequences. Do the same comparison inequalities hold over every complete local domain (where Yhee showed weakly lim Ulrich sequences can fail to exist)?
open_problems.reference: Iyengar-Ma-Walker, 'Lim Ulrich sequences and Boij-Soderberg cones', Forum Math. Sigma 11 (2023), arXiv:2209.03498; Yhee 2023 (non-existence of weakly lim Ulrich sequences); BEKS 2012
open_problems.status: open beyond rings with lim Ulrich sequences (as described in the 194 paper, main.tex:159-171; UNVERIFIED in the source)
open_problems.obstruction_match: Medium. The item replaces lim Ulrich sequences by a blowup pairing exactly for the H_0-length functional; Betti-cone inequalities need the whole family of Boij-Soderberg functionals, of which the item gives only the 'pure, equal-step' one.
open_problems.adaptation_sketch: Combine O1 (non-uniform steps) with Frobenius depth amplification to obtain local analogues of the Eisenbud-Schreyer facet functionals for each degree sequence; check whether they cut out the IMW comparison cone.

open_problems.title: Asymptotic Lech inequality in all characteristics (Huneke-Ma-Quy-Smirnov)
open_problems.statement: HMQS prove optimal Lech-type bounds e(I) vs l(R/I) for sufficiently deep m-primary ideals I (I contained in a high power of m) in characteristic p and conjecture them in all characteristics.
open_problems.reference: Huneke-Ma-Quy-Smirnov, 'Asymptotic Lech's inequality', Adv. Math. (2020), arXiv:1907.08344; related: Klein-Ma-Quy-Smirnov-Yao, arXiv:1808.01051 (Stuckrad-Vogel)
open_problems.status: open outside char p (snippet level; UNVERIFIED)
open_problems.obstruction_match: Weak. Same 'deep ideal' regime and same char-p normalized-length tools, but HMQS bound e(I) from above by colength for arbitrary I; the item bounds colength from below for ideals with deep finite FREE resolutions. Only for perfect ideals all of whose differentials are deep does the item say anything (l(R/I) >= e(R) s^d (1 - O(1/s))).
open_problems.adaptation_sketch: For perfect deep ideals, compare the item's lower bound with HMQS's optimal constant; for general I no route seen.

theorem_corollaries: Lech's conjecture e(R) <= e(S) for flat local maps, all characteristics (the paper's headline; not stated in Lean).
IMW 2022 Conj 8.1 for complete local domains of char p plus convergence of the Dutta sequence (the comparator OAI.Lech.dutta_domain).

Lean-only strengthening: dutta_complete_charp (DuttaDomain.lean:22) has no domain hypothesis, so the Lean proves chi_infty(F) >= e(R) for short complexes over EVERY complete Noetherian local ring of char p (the paper's Cor. is stated for domains; the prime-filtration step at charp.tex:269-310, which the paper uses after a residue-field extension, handles non-domains in the same way; Lean does exactly this in CyclicDutta.lean). Since chi_infty and e are unchanged by completion, this should extend to all char-p local rings (not stated in Lean).
The proof keeps the b_0 factor: chi_infty(F) >= rank(F_0) e(R) (charp.tex:244-253 before using b_0 >= 1).
IMW 2022's char-p Dutta bound for localized standard graded algebras, proved there via lim Ulrich sequences (speedup target 1).

IMW Length Conjecture l(M) >= beta_0(M) e(R) for char-p numerically Roberts rings, including all complete intersections (Dutta/Kurano chi_infty = chi). Whether the non-strict-CI case was known before is UNVERIFIED (speedup target 2).

Hilbert-Kunz consequence: e_HK(J) >= e(R) for every m-primary ideal J of finite projective dimension in a char-p local ring (Peskine-Szpiro gives H_i(Phi^n F) = 0 for i > 0, so chi_infty = e_HK(J)). Prior status UNVERIFIED.

Positivity of Dutta multiplicity in char p (Kurano-Roberts in char p) and the New Intersection Theorem in char p, as trivial weakenings; both have elementary proofs that do not need the device (negative_controls).
Ma 2017's bound e(R) <= max(1, d!/2^d) e(S), Lech in dimension 3 (equal char), Lech for standard graded sources (Ma 2023; Meng 2025): all subsumed by the headline.

Direct instances of Thm 2.1 with lambda = ordinary length over a Cohen-Macaulay local ring and I a minimal reduction: a local, asymptotic HHS-type bound l(M) >= e(R) s^d (beta_0 - A_d/s * sum beta_i) for finite-length modules of finite projective dimension whose whole minimal resolution has entries in m^{s+c}; equivalently a Betti-length trade-off (sum beta_i >= (s/A) beta_0 unless l(M) is within a factor (1-o(1)) of e(R) s^d beta_0). The graded analogue follows from Eisenbud-Schreyer; the local form appears new (UNVERIFIED). These are instances of the item, not reuse.

negative_controls.title: Ordinary Euler characteristic of short complexes over non-Roberts rings
negative_controls.statement: There are short complexes with chi(F) < 0 (Roberts) and modules with chi(M,N) = -1 over a non-regular ring (Dutta-Hochster-McLaughlin 1985).
negative_controls.reference: Dutta-Hochster-McLaughlin, Invent. Math. 79 (1985); Roberts' example as cited in arXiv:2404.17572
negative_controls.why: Proved-false analogue. The device must not give chi(F) >= e(R) for the ORDINARY Euler characteristic. In Lean, instantiating complex_estimate_basis with ordinary Module.length on such a ring must fail at the hypothesis _hK (positive Koszul homology of length zero) or _ha (exact a^h scaling), which hold for ordinary length only over CM rings. This also tests that the prover respects the length hypotheses rather than the shape of the conclusion.

negative_controls.title: Total rank / Generalized Total Rank Conjecture
negative_controls.statement: Sum of Betti numbers of a nonzero finite-length module of finite projective dimension is >= 2^d (Walker 2017 for char != 2; VandeBogert-Walker for char 2); the Generalized Total Rank Conjecture for complexes is FALSE in odd characteristic (Walker).
negative_controls.reference: Walker, Ann. Math. 186 (2017), arXiv:1702.02560; VandeBogert-Walker, arXiv:2305.09771
negative_controls.why: The ranks b_i enter the item only through the O(1/s) error and disappear in the Frobenius limit, so the item gives no Betti lower bound. A prover with the item should show no speedup on Walker's theorem; a claimed 'proof' of the false generalized version via the item would expose a misuse.

negative_controls.title: New Intersection Theorem and Dutta positivity in char p
negative_controls.statement: A finite free complex of length k < dim R with finite-length homology has H_0 = 0; chi_infty(F) > 0 for short complexes.
negative_controls.why: Coefficient 1 is not needed: H_0(Phi^n F) surjects onto (R/m^[q])^{b_0}, so l >= c q^d, while Roberts' Frobenius homology bound (in OAI: frobenius_quotient_homology_bound, FrobeniusHomologyGrowth.lean:46) gives O(q^k). With or without the item the Lean proof is short glue, so the expected speedup is about zero. Statable now; a cheap check that the harness does not credit the device for easy consequences.

negative_controls.title: Hilbert-Kunz Lech (Kunz) and Watanabe-Yoshida
negative_controls.statement: e_HK(R) <= e_HK(S) for flat local maps in char p (Kunz 1976, classical); Watanabe-Yoshida lower bound e_HK(R) >= e_HK(R_{p,d}) for non-regular R (open in general).
negative_controls.reference: Kunz, Amer. J. Math. 98 (1976); Enescu-Shimomoto, arXiv:math/0502289
negative_controls.why: No complex with deep entries is involved: Kunz's inequality is elementary, and the Watanabe-Yoshida bound concerns e_HK of the ring itself. The device should not help either.

negative_controls.title: Tightness control (not a negative control): Koszul complexes
negative_controls.statement: F = K(z_1^s, ..., z_h^s; C): b_0 = 1, sum b_i = 2^h, lambda H_0 = mu s^h exactly.
negative_controls.why: The bound mu s^h (1 - A 2^h/s) matches to leading order, so coefficient 1 cannot be improved. Use it to sanity-check any proposed generalization (O1) or rediscovery.

top5.title: O1: local pure-type estimate with non-uniform depths s_1..s_h
top5.argument: The only Lean-statable target found where the device's DESIGN, not just its statement, must be reused. The graded analogue is the Herzog-Kuhl formula / HHS lower bound, but no local version in terms of m-adic depth of the differentials was found. Arm C (statement plus sum_estimate, rootTotal_euler_nonnegative and the root numerics) should make it a re-parametrization (new twists O(-d_i), new root rule, new layer polynomial), while arm A has no visible route: the associated-graded passage loses exactness. Caveat: it is a generalization of the item itself, so a success is weaker evidence than reuse on an independent famous problem.

top5.title: Speedup 1: IMW 2022 standard-graded Dutta bound (calibration)
top5.lean: statable with < 300 lines of new definitions
top5.argument: A known 45-page lim-Ulrich theorem that becomes completion glue plus dutta_complete_charp. It does not count as device reuse (it is a corollary of the comparator theorem), but it is the cleanest measurable before/after pair for the harness and shows that the device subsumes the lim-Ulrich route on its own home ground.

top5.title: O2: IMW Length Conjecture l(M) >= e(R)
top5.argument: Statable now with Mathlib (Module.length, projective dimension, depth) and OAI multiplicity. The char-p numerically Roberts case is a corollary, so the informative experiment is the general case: whether a prover with the item finds any non-Frobenius depth amplification. Expect failure; a failure is informative about the device's scope (it controls Dutta multiplicity, not length).

top5.title: Negative control: New Intersection Theorem in char p
top5.argument: Statable now with IsShortComplex-style hypotheses; the elementary proof (Frobenius surjection onto (R/m^[q])^{b_0} plus the OAI Frobenius growth bound) does not need coefficient 1. A harness that reports a large speedup here is miscalibrated.

top5.title: O3: Kurano-Roberts positivity and IMW Conj 8.1 in mixed characteristic
top5.argument: The strongest genuine reuse candidate mathematically: the same inequality where Frobenius is unavailable, and the paper already runs Thm 2.1 with perfectoid lengths for Lech. Not Lean-usable (no local Chern characters, no perfectoid lengths in the OAI library), so it can only be tested informally.
